prompt:
Image 1 is a grey clay maquette of this figure: follow its pose, its parts and its framing, the whole figure from head to foot filling the square as it does, seen three-quarter front from a little above. It is a crude blockout: take its pose, its parts and its framing, not its stubby proportions. Paint over it completely: no grey clay and no plain smooth shapes may remain. Image 2 is a style reference only: match its painting style, brushwork, candle lighting, rim light, muted colours and dark background. Do not copy its head-and-shoulders framing. The subject, its face, its headgear and every ornament must follow the description below exactly; do not copy the man, the helm, the horns, the fur or the trim from Image 2.

A full-length painted portrait of the Primordial, a colossal ancient beast-god from before the world was young, slow and vast, in a regal pose: standing four-square, head lifted high and turned a little toward the right, chest out, the club tail resting on the ground behind. Three-quarter front view, the body and the face turned slightly toward the right side of the image. Square image. Framing: the whole figure fills the height of the square: the top of the horns about 6% from the top edge and the feet about 94% from the top, centred, with dark empty space around the silhouette. One figure only: no people, no worshippers, no other creatures, no text, no border, no frame, no signature, no logo.
Lighting: a single warm candle key light from the upper left, a dim warm fill, deep warm shadows, and a thin soft warm rim light along the horns, the humped back and the moss that separates the whole silhouette clearly from the background. As in the style reference, much of the figure falls into deep warm shadow: the candle picks out the upper left of the head, the shoulders and the chest, and the lower body and the far side sink into the dark; it is not evenly lit. Background: plain, unpatterned, very dark warm brown close to #1C1A17, with no objects, no landscape, no horizon and no floor: the dark background runs unbroken to the bottom edge, with only a faint soft shadow under the feet.
Medium: painterly oil on a wood panel, loose visible brushwork and soft edges as in the style reference, moderate detail, never a crisp, clean digital illustration; a strong readable silhouette: the shape of the ram's horns, the humped mossy back and the club tail against the dark background must still read when the image is shrunk to 64 pixels.
Colors: muted and earthy. The one clear colour of the beast is the moss on its back: crusted with a dull ember-orange lichen (#C4532C), the Cinder Horde's colour. Nothing in the image glows. No other saturated area larger than a small clasp or trim.

Subject: Body: a massive, heavy four-legged beast like a great primeval bull crossed with a giant ground sloth, with a deep chest, a high humped back and thick pillar legs with blunt claws; its hide is brown (#7A5638), thick and wrinkled, mottled with irregular patches of lichen grey-green (#909080). Head: a broad, heavy head with small deep-set dark eyes and a blunt muzzle. Horns: a pair of huge curling ram's horns spiralling around the sides of its head. Back: its hump and spine are overgrown with a thick mantle of moss, crusted with a dull ember-orange lichen (#C4532C), the Cinder Horde's colour. Tail: a short thick tail ending in a heavy bony club.
Paint it as described, the whole figure clearly in view.
